sections.title: Executive Summary
sections.guide: 1-2 paragraphs: what the product is, the central claim of this document, and how value is created and captured.

sections.title: Strategic Thesis
sections.guide: The underlying bet or belief, stated plainly (an if/then sentence or 2-3 numbered pillars).

sections.title: Core Principles
sections.guide: 3-5 principles as '- **Name:** explanation' bullets, each traceable to evidence.

sections.title: Product Expression
sections.guide: Where the thesis shows up concretely: named surfaces, features, deployment options, named customers and results.

sections.title: Tradeoffs and Boundaries
sections.guide: What the product deliberately does not do, what it sacrifices, and who it is not for.

sections.title: Implementation Implications
sections.guide: Consequences for product, engineering, GTM or deployment teams that follow from the above.

sections.title: Executive Summary
sections.guide: Who this customer/persona is in one paragraph and why they matter to the product.

sections.title: Primary Profile
sections.guide: '- **Label:** value' bullets (e.g. Company Type & Industry, Company Size, Team & Function, Operating Maturity; or Role & Title, Reporting Line, Responsibilities, Success Metrics).

sections.title: Evidence-Backed Attributes
sections.guide: Attributes inferred from concrete signals (case studies, contact-form fields, job posts, docs). Name the signal.

sections.title: Needs and Constraints
sections.guide: Split into ### Needs and ### Constraints, 3-4 bold-labelled bullets each.

sections.title: Decision Implications
sections.guide: What this profile implies for sales motion, onboarding, product scope and messaging.

sections.title: Boundaries and Disqualifiers
sections.guide: Who is explicitly a poor fit and why.

sections.title: Executive Summary
sections.guide: The demand dynamic this document models, in 1-2 paragraphs.

sections.title: Core Model
sections.guide: The central tension and the model itself (numbered causal stack, JTBD statements, outcome list, alternatives list - depending on the document).

sections.title: Causal Structure
sections.guide: The chain of causes behind the model as a numbered or bulleted list with bold lead-ins.

sections.title: Triggers and Context
sections.guide: The conditions and moments where the model becomes active; numbered ### subsections when the document is about triggers.

sections.title: Customer Consequences
sections.guide: What happens to the customer if the problem persists or the outcome is reached.

sections.title: Product Implications
sections.guide: How the product architecture answers the model (name real surfaces/features).

sections.title: Executive Summary
sections.guide: The positioning claim this document describes, in 1-2 paragraphs.

sections.title: Strategic Definition
sections.guide: The precise definition (for Category: declared, evaluation and emergent/owned layers as a numbered list).

sections.title: Audience and Frame of Reference
sections.guide: Split into ### Target Audience and ### Frame of Reference (the alternatives buyers compare against).

sections.title: Value and Differentiation
sections.guide: Structural differentiators with bold lead-ins; numbered ### subsections allowed in Positioning.

sections.title: Supporting Proof
sections.guide: Named customers, exact metrics, funding, partnerships - copied verbatim from the facts ledger.

sections.title: Strategic Implications
sections.guide: What the positioning enables or requires going forward.

sections.title: Executive Summary
sections.guide: The competitive logic in 1-2 paragraphs, including the alternatives the product is compared against.

sections.title: Strategic Model
sections.guide: How the company competes, as 3-4 bold-labelled bullets.

sections.title: Advantage or Switching Stack
sections.guide: Competitive Advantage Stack: a table with columns Advantage Dimension | Description | Buyer Consequence | Uniqueness | Evidence | Score / Strength. Switching Strategy: a numbered list of switching-cost neutralizers.

sections.title: Buyer Consequences
sections.guide: What the buyer gets or avoids because of the stack.

sections.title: Reinforcing Mechanisms
sections.guide: The flywheel: a numbered list where each advantage feeds the next.

sections.title: Risks and Limits
sections.guide: Where the stack is fragile or does not hold.

sections.title: Executive Summary
sections.guide: The commercial reality in 1-2 paragraphs; say explicitly whether prices are public.

sections.title: Commercial Architecture
sections.guide: How the offer is sold and contracted (self-serve vs. sales-led, contract shape, dimensions that drive contract value).

sections.title: Value and Scaling Logic
sections.guide: What makes the bill grow and why that tracks customer value.

sections.title: Packaging and Boundaries
sections.guide: Tiers, editions, add-ons, deployment options, services and what is gated where.

sections.title: Expansion Mechanics
sections.guide: How revenue expands inside an account (use cases, units, geographies).

sections.title: Risks and Tradeoffs
sections.guide: Misalignment risks of the model and the tradeoffs accepted.

sections.title: Executive Summary
sections.guide: The go-to-market motion in 1-2 paragraphs: sales-led vs. product-led, deal shape, who sells to whom.

sections.title: Motion Model
sections.guide: Entry point, sales cycle shape, deal size signals, self-serve vs. demo/contact flows.

sections.title: Buyer Journey and Stages
sections.guide: Numbered stages from first touch to expansion, grounded in observable steps (forms, demos, pilots, phases).

sections.title: Roles and Channels
sections.guide: Sales/deployment roles (careers pages are good evidence), partners, regional presence, events, marketplaces.

sections.title: Proof and Enablement
sections.guide: Assets used to sell: case studies, ROI claims, trials/pilots, content, certifications.

sections.title: Risks and Tradeoffs
sections.guide: Constraints of the motion (cycle length, cost of sale, scalability).

sections.title: Executive Summary
sections.guide: The messaging/brand system this document describes in 1-2 paragraphs.

sections.title: Core System
sections.guide: The system itself (levels, term groups, pains/outcomes/objections - see per-document shape).

sections.title: Patterns and Hierarchy
sections.guide: How the elements are ordered and recur; numbered levels or ### subsections.

sections.title: Representative Evidence
sections.guide: Verbatim quotes from the source, as bullets in double quotes. Never paraphrase here.

sections.title: Usage Rules
sections.guide: Do/don't rules derived from the evidence, with bold lead-ins.

sections.title: Application Guidance
sections.guide: How to apply the system when writing copy, docs or briefs.

sections.title: Purpose
sections.guide: 1-2 sentences: what the feature enables and why it exists.

sections.title: Users and Jobs
sections.guide: '- **Role**: job' bullets (humans and, if relevant, agents/systems).

sections.title: Functional Requirements
sections.guide: 3-6 requirements, '- **FRn: Name**: description' or bold-labelled bullets.

sections.title: Flows
sections.guide: Numbered flows (creation, execution, monitoring...) with arrows for step sequences.

sections.title: States
sections.guide: Lifecycle states as '- `State`: meaning'.

sections.title: Edge Cases
sections.guide: Failure and boundary scenarios with expected handling.

sections.title: Data Considerations
sections.guide: Storage, retention, encryption, limits, audit.

sections.title: Security and Privacy
sections.guide: Access control, isolation, secrets, PII.

sections.title: Accessibility
sections.guide: WCAG-level expectations for the feature's UI (or CLI equivalents).

sections.title: Acceptance Criteria
sections.guide: Testable criteria, 'AC-n:' style allowed.

sections.title: Non-Goals
sections.guide: What the feature explicitly will not do.

categories.name: Product Strategy
categories.label: Estratégia de produto
categories.blurb: Tese, princípios, gosto de produto, casos de uso centrais e lógica de expansão.

docs.title: Core Use Cases
docs.focus: The concrete workflows/jobs where the product is used in production, clustered by industry or function, with named customers and outcomes.

docs.title: Expansion Logic
docs.focus: How the product enters an account (entry wedge) and expands: adjacent workflows, business lines, geographies, ownership handover.

docs.title: Product Principles
docs.focus: The decision rules behind the product. Core Principles must be 3-5 '### N. Prefer X over Y' subsections, each with '* **Operational Rule:**' and '* **Context:**' bullets.

docs.title: Product Taste
docs.focus: The product's stance on density, interaction style, copy/terminology and onboarding; tradeoffs such as opinionated vs. configurable, speed vs. ceremony, expert vs. novice.

docs.title: Product Thesis
docs.focus: The core bet. Strategic Thesis must contain one 'If ..., then ... must ..., producing ...' sentence followed by 2-3 numbered pillars.

categories.name: Customers
categories.label: Clientes
categories.blurb: ICP, persona compradora e persona usuária.

docs.title: Buyer Persona
docs.focus: The economic buyer and champion: titles, mandate, KPIs, buying criteria, objections, how they evaluate.

docs.title: ICP
docs.focus: The ideal customer at company level: industry, size, function, operating maturity, tech/infra requirements, disqualifiers.

docs.title: User Persona
docs.focus: The day-to-day users (one primary archetype, optionally secondary ones): workflows, tools touched, needs, frustrations.

categories.name: Problems & Demand
categories.label: Problemas e demanda
categories.blurb: Modelo de problema, JTBD, resultados desejados, gatilhos de compra e troca, alternativas atuais.

docs.title: Buying Triggers
docs.focus: Events and thresholds that start a purchase. Triggers and Context should use numbered '### N. Trigger Name' subsections.

docs.title: Current Alternatives
docs.focus: What customers do today instead (DIY/in-house, incumbents, services firms, status quo) and why each falls short.

docs.title: Desired Outcomes
docs.focus: Measurable outcomes customers want, with the metrics the company itself uses (exact figures from the ledger).

docs.title: Jobs to Be Done
docs.focus: Core Model must contain 3-5 JTBD statements in the form '- **When** ..., **I want to** ..., **so I can** ...'; also functional, emotional and social jobs.

docs.title: Problem Model
docs.focus: Core Model as a numbered causal stack: Surface Symptom, Underlying Operational Mechanism, Business Consequence, Emotional and Strategic Consequence.

docs.title: Switching Triggers
docs.focus: What makes customers abandon their current solution for this one. Triggers and Context should use numbered '### N. Trigger Name' subsections.

categories.name: Market & Positioning
categories.label: Mercado e posicionamento
categories.blurb: Categoria, posicionamento, promessa de valor, diferenciação e visão de mercado.

docs.title: Category
docs.focus: Strategic Definition must list three layers: 1. Declared Category, 2. Evaluation Category, 3. Emergent/Owned Category.

docs.title: Differentiation
docs.focus: What is structurally different versus the frame of reference, and the proof for each difference.

docs.title: Market Worldview
docs.focus: The company's belief about how the market is changing: the old way vs. the new way and why now.

docs.title: Positioning
docs.focus: Classic positioning: for whom, against what, the numbered differentiators ('### N. Name' under Value and Differentiation) and proof.

docs.title: Value Promise
docs.focus: The core promise to the customer, what it commits to, and the evidence that it is kept.

categories.name: Competition & Market Dynamics
categories.label: Competição
categories.blurb: Pilha de vantagens competitivas e estratégia de troca.

docs.title: Competitive Advantage Stack
docs.focus: Advantage or Switching Stack must be a table: Advantage Dimension | Description | Buyer Consequence | Uniqueness | Evidence | Score / Strength (dimensions such as Product, Service, Trust & Architecture, Distribution, Data & R&D).

docs.title: Switching Strategy
docs.focus: How the company lowers switching costs and displaces incumbents; Advantage or Switching Stack as a numbered list of neutralizers.

categories.name: Pricing & Monetization
categories.label: Preço e monetização
categories.blurb: Modelo de preço, métrica de valor, empacotamento e filosofia de monetização.

docs.title: Monetization Philosophy
docs.focus: The company's beliefs about what it charges for and why; what it refuses to charge for.

docs.title: Packaging
docs.focus: How the offer is bundled: plans/editions, add-ons, deployment options, services, and gating.

docs.title: Pricing Model
docs.focus: The price structure (subscription, usage, seats, contracts). Public prices copied exactly with currency and period; if none are published, say so in the Executive Summary.

docs.title: Value Metric
docs.focus: The unit that should scale price with customer value: list candidates, assess each, and mark inferred candidates.

categories.name: Sales & GTM
categories.label: Vendas e GTM
categories.blurb: Motion de vendas, jornada do comprador, papéis e canais.

docs.title: Sales Motion
docs.focus: How the company finds, sells to and expands customers: motion model, buyer journey stages, roles and channels, proof assets.

categories.name: Messaging & Brand
categories.label: Mensagem e marca
categories.blurb: Hierarquia de mensagens, narrativa, voz, léxico e linguagem do cliente.

docs.title: Brand Narrative
docs.focus: The story arc (old world, tension, new way, proof). Patterns and Hierarchy must have ### Narrative Pillars and ### Voice and Tone.

docs.title: Brand Voice
docs.focus: Voice attributes, tone shifts by context, sentence-level patterns, do/don't.

docs.title: Customer Language
docs.focus: How customers describe pains, outcomes and objections. Prefer attributed customer quotes; if the language comes mostly from the company's own copy, add an 'evidence' caveat saying so.

docs.title: Messaging Hierarchy
docs.focus: Core System as six levels.

docs.title: Vocabulary / Lexicon
docs.focus: Core System as seven term groups, each a list of '- **Term:** definition' bullets.

categories.name: Features
categories.label: Funcionalidades
categories.blurb: Funcionalidades da plataforma e modelos de deployment.
